content.content:
## Sandbox Profiles

The Who can see what card is a small grid, so each run's reach is seen at a glance: the project's areas down its left, Code, Spec source, Compiled reference, Project data, and Everything else, and the modes across its top, Code, Spec, Ask, and Freeform, each in its mode's colour. Each cell is a small label: "Edit", on a faint tint of the theme's success colour; "Read", on a faint tint of its accent; or "No access", muted and untinted. Hovering a cell shows the paths it covers. Beneath the grid, one muted line says what every mode can reach outside the project, as "System and toolchains read only; the harness's folders, build caches, and a temporary folder editable". The grid follows the classification and the Spec tasks switches as they change, so a change shows at once what it allows.
The grid is editable, for the open project: clicking a cell opens a small menu beneath it of Edit, Read, and No access, the cell's level ticked, and picking one sets it, the cell changing at once and the project's profiles following, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says. Each cell the user has set is marked with a small dot in its corner, and its menu has "Use default" too, which puts back what the profile gives it by default. Only what the sandbox can enforce is offered: a choice that would let a Code run read the spec source, or a Spec run change the code, is shown disabled in its menu, its tooltip saying the separation of code and spec is never relaxed, Project data can never be given Edit, and Ask can never be given Edit anywhere. A "Reset grid" button beneath the grid, enabled while any cell is set, puts every cell back to its default. Each change is saved to `.suspense/sandbox.json` straight away and takes effect from the next run. Setting the Code row to Read in the Spec column is the same as the Spec tasks card's "Read the code" switch, and setting Everything else to Read there the same as "Read the whole project", so the switches and the grid always agree.

## Sandbox Classification

The Code and spec card says, muted, which parts of the project are code and which are spec, and that a Code run can't open spec and a Spec run can't open code. It holds two lists side by side, "Code", headed in Code's colour, and "Spec", in Spec's, each a column of rows, one per folder or pattern, in monospace, with a small remove button at its right shown on hover. Beneath each list, "Add folder" opens the folder browser in the project, and "Add pattern" adds a row to type a pattern into, as `**/*.pi`, saved once Enter is pressed or it loses focus. A row in both lists is marked in the theme's error colour in each, with a line beneath the card saying runs won't start until it is in one only. At the card's foot, a small ghost "Reset to project locations" button is enabled only while the lists differ from the project's code and spec locations. Each change is saved to `.suspense/sandbox.json` straight away, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says.

## Sandbox Spec Tasks

The Spec tasks card holds two switches, each a row with its label at the left, a muted line under it saying what it does, and the switch at the right: "Read the code", saying Spec tasks can read the code but never change it, and, indented beneath it and shown only while it is on, "Read the whole project", saying they can also read the rest of the project, read only. Both start off, are saved with the project, and take effect from the next run.

## Sandbox Outside
## Classification

Which paths are code and which are spec is the project's to say, in `.suspense/sandbox.json`, saved with its data, as the [ProjectData](../project-data/index.md#project-data) says, and edited in the [SettingsWindow](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window)'s Sandbox section. It holds a list of code roots and a list of spec roots, each a path in the project, and patterns classing files anywhere as code or spec, as `**/*.pi` for spec, so a project laid out in any way, with several roots, or spec and code side by side, can be classed. With no file, the project's code location is its only code root and its spec location its only spec root, as the [ProjectLocations](../project-locations/index.md#project-locations) says. A path classed as both is a contradiction, and runs refuse until it is resolved; a path classed as neither is denied to Code and Spec runs alike, and readable by questions. The profiles are built from the classification each time a run starts, so a change takes effect from the next run.
The same file holds the project's own levels for each profile, as set in the [SettingsWindow](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window)'s grid: for each mode and each area of the project, code, spec source, compiled reference, project data, and everything else, Edit, Read, or No access, where it differs from the profile's default. They are applied over the defaults when the profile is built, and never past what the sandbox allows: a level that would let a Code run read the spec's source, a Spec run change the code, a Question run change anything, or any run change the project's data, is refused when the policy is compiled, as a contradiction, and the run doesn't start until it is put right.

content.text:
The "Who can see what" grid in Settings → Sandbox is now editable for the open project. Clicking a cell opens a menu of Edit, Read and No access with the current level ticked, and the change saves to `.suspense/sandbox.json` at once and applies from the next run.

- **Changed cells:** they get a small dot, and their menu adds "Use default". A "Reset grid" button below the grid is enabled while any cell is changed and puts them all back.
- **Limits:** the forbidden choices are greyed out:
  - a Code run reading the spec source;
  - a Spec run editing the code;
  - Edit anywhere for Ask;
  - Edit for project data in any mode.

  If one of these somehow ends up in `sandbox.json` (for example, edited by hand), the profile is refused and the run doesn't start.
- **Linked to the switches:** the Spec column's Code cell *is* the "Read the code" switch. Its Everything else cell at Read is "Read the whole project", so the grid and the switches always agree.
- **Reset to project locations:** it now only compares and resets the code and spec lists, leaving the grid's levels alone.

**Where I departed from the spec:** the spec asks for a tooltip on the greyed-out choices explaining why. The menu component has no tooltips on items, so the reasons appear as plain lines at the bottom of the menu instead.

**Not run in the project folder:** as last time, this session's own sandbox blocks the files Suspense's build needs. I type-checked and tested a copy with those prompt files stubbed. There the build has no warnings, and all 20 sandbox and settings tests pass, including new ones for the levels and the editable grid.
